recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if the Patient notes lose this paragraph or a later Applied/Published PA decision changes the MRN request approach; broader identifier profiling or registry guidance belongs under later issues such as FHIR-48692 or successors.
issue_request: FHIR-14099 was a Published FHIR-core Patient issue, resolved Persuasive for STU3, asking for consistent guidance on how a client can request creation of a new identifier such as an MRN. The accepted resolution directed that the Patient ids and Patient resource ids section describe using an identifier with assigner, MRN type and/or system, and no value so internal business rules can populate the actual identifier.
initial_application: Commit dfe2cd1c803a8430f4175cbc3b2c105db227ded6, titled "GF#14099: Guidance on how to request a new identifier", added the accepted paragraph to source/patient/patient-notes.xml. Later Patient notes work, including FHIR-48396 commit 54897cd3ffc4c700392ddae3204b41627e63b561, preserved that paragraph while changing adjacent Patient linkage and operation-link text.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Patient as an active PA-owned resource, making source/patient/patient-notes.xml build-scoped Patient narrative source. The originating Zulip thread considered operation, data absent reason, no-value assigner/type/system, and Identifier.use approaches, and PA did not pursue a new Identifier.use code. A later PA Confluence identifier page references FHIR-14099 and broader identifier issues but remains consistent with the seed guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was needed because source/patient/patient-notes.xml already contains the requested section heading and MRN request paragraph.
